about: Wattle and daub's frame (D236, D258, tools/kits): one member of squared oak, adzed, laid by the frame's rule as each post, plate, rail, brace and stud and scaled across to its size; open along it so copies run on as one timber, closed where it stops by its sawn end.

member.about: A squared oak timber hewn by axe and adze, modelled; laid as every post, plate, rail, brace and stud of the frame, scaled across to its size.
